reason: M8 is diode-connected and mainly serves to bias net013 (and effectively bias M9’s gate); removing it often leaves the signal devices still present but eliminates the self-bias/reference at net013. Caveat: you must provide an external bias for net013 (or directly for M9’s gate) or the operating point can become undefined.
impact_estimate: Low-to-moderate (functional path remains, but DC bias stability is reduced unless replaced)

reason: M3 is a self-gated NMOS at VOUT1 (diode-connected / clamp-like behavior) that likely provides local feedback, clamping, or output bias stabilization rather than being essential to the differential input device (M1). Caveat: removing it can shift the output common-mode and increase output swing/nonlinearity, so you may need another mechanism to keep VOUT1 in range.
impact_estimate: Low-to-moderate (core amplification via M1+load can remain; output bias/swing behavior changes)

reason: M9 is the PMOS active load/pull-up for VOUT1; if your definition of “functionality” is preserving the input NMOS transconductor action (M1) rather than producing a defined high-gain output node, M9 can be removed and VOUT1 can be treated as an internal node. Caveat: without M9 (or another pull-up/load), VOUT1 will float or sit near VSS, so you’ll need a replacement load if you still need a valid output voltage.
impact_estimate: Low if a defined VOUT1 output is not required; moderate if VOUT1 must be a usable amplified output
